text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov said he opposed a draft bill submitted to parliament which bans former communist leaders from holding senior state posts. @

-- Bulgaria has sent a formal request to Germany's government authorities to clear speculation about alleged Bulgaria's involvement in a 1981 attempt to kill Pope Joan Paul II, following publications in the German press, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

-- Bulgaria will seek foreign consultants for restructuring its state firms in a move to bring them closer to international production and marketing standards, deputy Prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria's state tobacco monopolist Bulgartabak said it would seek 300 billion levs to fund purchasing of this year's tobacco crop seen at around 80,000 tonnes.

-- Bulgaria is expected to seek restructuring of Bulgarian-Russian joint gas firm Topenergy if private shareholders were not excluded from the company, deputy Prime minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said. @

Russia's Gazprom holds 50 percent in Topenergy, Bulgarian private firm Overgas Inc holds 8.5 percent, Bulgaria's private business conglomerate Multigroup also has 8.5 percent, the state Bulgargas has 25.1 percent and the remainder is held by two Bulgarian banks and a private company.
-- Bulgaria is facing a syphilis outbreak, Health Ministry officials said after the ministry registered 916 new cases of syphilis in the country in the first half of 1997.
-- Bulgaria's Transport ministry said it had replaced the head of Sofia Airport Danyo Adanev with Zdravko Velichkov, a former chief of state carrier Hemus Air.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved a declaration aking equal start for the East European countries in the process of their integration into the European Union. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
